title: Interfaces for augmented ring complexes and ordered localization models
statement: Use modules on the one-object bottom-topology site [def-pc-ring-hom-extension-shared-definitions], integer cochain complexes, and the ordinary derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For a commutative ring $A$, write $A[0]$ for its unit module in degree zero. A ring-complex family consists of complexes $K(A,I)$ for finitely generated ideals $I\subset A$, augmentations $\epsilon_{A,I}:K(A,I)\to A[0]$, and degreewise $\varphi$-semilinear maps $m_\varphi:K(A,I)\to K(B,J)$ whenever $\varphi:A\to B$ and $\varphi(I)B=J$. The predicate $\operatorname{RingComplexFunctorial}$ is the conjunction $m_\varphi d=d m_\varphi$, $\epsilon_{B,J}m_\varphi=\varphi\epsilon_{A,I}$, $m_{\mathrm{id}}=\mathrm{id}$, and $m_\psi m_\varphi=m_{\psi\varphi}$, including every equality witness for ideal extension. For an ideal $I\subset A$ and augmented complex $(K,\epsilon)$, the predicate $\operatorname{RingComplexHasCechModel}(A,I,K,\epsilon)$ says that every finite list $f:\{1,\ldots,r\}\to A$ spanning $I$ has an augmented complex $(C,a)$ with $C^n=0$ for $n<0$, an $A$-linear identification $C^0\cong A$, and $A$-linear identifications $C^{q+1}\cong\prod_{i_0<\cdots<i_q}A[1/(f_{i_0}\cdots f_{i_q})]$ for $q\geq0$, using [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. The first differential sends $x$ to its images in each localization; later differentials are $\sum_j(-1)^j$ times the face localization maps. The augmentation $a:C\to A[0]$ is the degree-zero identification. There is an isomorphism $\alpha:C\cong K$ in $D(A)$ with $\epsilon\alpha=a$. Empty lists are included. These predicates select no objects. The proved transport lemma sends such a model backwards along any quasi-isomorphism $p:P\to K$, with augmentation $\epsilon p$.
